malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Kronos banking Trojan code (not shown in report, but referenced as credential stealing and banking malware)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code injects itself into browser processes, intercepts user credentials entered into banking websites, and exfiltrates them to a remote command-and-control server, enabling credential theft and financial fraud.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting user credentials and exfiltrating them is a hallmark of banking malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software should not inject into browser processes or steal user credentials.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Penetration testing tools may simulate similar actions in controlled environments.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Cerber ransomware code (not shown in report, but referenced as ransomware with credential and cryptocurrency theft features)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code encrypts user files, harvests private credentials from web browsers, and attempts to steal cryptocurrency wallet information, then sends this data to a remote server, resulting in data loss and financial theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Encrypting user files and stealing credentials/cryptocurrency is highly malicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not encrypt user files or steal sensitive data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup software may access files, but not encrypt for ransom or exfiltrate credentials.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Svpeng Android banking Trojan code (not shown in report, but referenced as keylogger using Accessibility Services)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code abuses Android Accessibility Services to log keystrokes and capture sensitive information, then sends the data to a remote server, enabling credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Abusing Accessibility Services for keylogging is a common malware tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps should not use Accessibility Services for keylogging.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Accessibility features for users with disabilities, but not for data theft.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious Chrome extension code (not shown in report, but referenced as distributing adware and potentially hijacking user sessions)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code injects ads into web pages and may hijack user sessions or redirect traffic, resulting in adware distribution and potential credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Hijacking browser extensions to inject ads or steal data is a known attack vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate extensions should not inject unauthorized ads or steal user data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Ad blockers or productivity tools may modify web pages, but not for malicious gain.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Dumbo tool code (not shown in report, but referenced as suspending webcam processes and deleting/manipulating video recordings)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code suspends processes using webcams and deletes or manipulates video recordings, enabling anti-forensics and evidence destruction.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Disabling surveillance and deleting evidence is a clear sign of anti-forensic activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not tamper with surveillance or evidence.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security tools may disable cameras for privacy, but not for evidence destruction.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Steganography code (not shown in report, but referenced as hiding data in images for C&C or payload delivery)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hides malicious payloads or C&C instructions within image files, then extracts and executes them, enabling covert communication and payload delivery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Hiding code or C&C data in images is a known evasion technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal image files should not contain executable code or C&C instructions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Digital watermarking, but not for malware delivery.

attack_chain.action: Initial infection via phishing, exploit kit, or malicious download.
Malware executes and performs credential theft, keylogging, or ad injection.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of sensitive data or financial theft.

attack_chain.action: Malware encrypts files or manipulates system for ransom or anti-forensics.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data loss, ransom demand, or evidence destruction.

attack_chain.action: Malware communicates with C&C using covert channels (e.g., steganography).
attack_chain.leads_to: Sustained control or further payload delivery.

behavioral_signatures: Abuse of Accessibility Services for keylogging
Browser extension code modification and ad injection
File encryption and ransom note creation
Webcam process suspension and video file deletion
Extraction of data from image files (steganography)
file_indicators: Unusual access to browser credential stores
Chrome extension updates from untrusted sources
Creation of ransom notes or encrypted file extensions
Deletion or manipulation of video surveillance files
Image files with appended or hidden payloads
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known C2 infrastructure
Unusual POST requests containing credentials or cryptocurrency wallet data
Covert C&C via image file uploads/downloads
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for process injection, credential store access, and abuse of Accessibility Services. Watch for unauthorized Chrome extension updates and ad injection. Detect file encryption activity and ransom note creation. Alert on webcam process suspension and video file deletion. Analyze image files for hidden payloads or C&C data. Correlate with outbound network connections to suspicious domains or C2 infrastructure.
